_comment: The weights ARE the strategy, and they are not AI output (PRODUCT D6/H5). They live here rather than in the UI so they stay a visible, version-controlled artifact that a PM owns and a reviewer can diff. Changing a number here re-bands every problem immediately and with no model call — the factors are stored, the arithmetic is deterministic.

_rationale.customerValue+strategicFit: 0.70 of the total, because PRODUCT D2 says prioritisation is weighted by customer value and strategic fit. Together they have to be able to outvote breadth, or the system reproduces the vote-counting it exists to replace.
_rationale.evidenceStrength: 0.20 deliberately, not more. Breadth of corroboration is the input that was ALREADY dominant in the spreadsheet this replaces — 'vote count is the only quantified field, so it dominates by default' (PRODUCT, prioritisation pain). Giving it minority weight is the whole point; a widely-felt problem that touches no goal should be visibly ranked below a narrow one that does.
_rationale.effort: 0.10, the smallest weight, because it is the factor the model is worst at. The prompt tells it to expect to be wrong here. A low weight means a bad effort guess cannot swing a band on its own. Note the direction: 1 means cheap, so a higher score raises priority.
_rationale.bands: Cut points, not a curve. Bands rather than ranks because 7.4 vs 7.1 is noise dressed as rigor (PRODUCT challenge #4), and a PM shown a decimal rubber-stamps it. w2 re-cut now and next so a boundary never splits a cluster of near-identical scores: both sit in the widest gaps in the measured distribution of 23 problems — 0.80 in the 0.815/0.780 gap among the leaders, 0.65 in the 0.665/0.520 gap that separates the real candidates from the tail — which puts 4 problems in now instead of w1's 10. Ten of 23 in now is not a prioritisation. `later` is unchanged at 0.35. These cut points are chosen from the score distribution and nothing in this build measures whether they are right; the eval harness scores dedupe, not bands.
